content:
The assembly experience for the Prusa CORE One KIT was quite good overall. The instructions were very clear, and as long as you followed the steps one by one, there were generally no major issues.

In comparison, the assembly instructions for upgrading the CORE One to both GEN2 and INDX at the same time are quite poor. They require a lot of repeatedly switching between different pages, which is particularly inconvenient for users working in an offline environment.

Would it be possible to provide a PDF document with a complete, step-by-step guide for upgrading the CORE One to both GEN2 and INDX simultaneously? Having a comprehensive guide that can be downloaded and read offline would be greatly appreciated and is really needed.

As others have stated, +1 to this being a suboptimal guide and build experience.

I’ve been upgrading since the original MK3, including every upgrade and MMU generation, and I’ve never been this confused. Part of the Prusa experience is imho the build itself and getting to know every part of the printer while assembling it. That was always fun for me.

This build is not fun. It’s a constant struggle to figure out whether I’m still on track or have missed a crucial step across the multiple parallel guides.

I understand that setting up these guides involves a lot of work, but I’d argue that creating separate guides for separate build paths would reduce complexity for Prusa as well.

I would appreciate it if Prusa returned to its roots when it comes to quality and the build experience.

I am also confused.   I bought and assembled a Core One with MMU and got the INDX upgrade and it seems there is the C1+ to C1+ Gen2 upgrade included.  What is the best couse of actions for upgrading and installing of these?  Do I have to upgrade to the plus version first?  Is there a kit for this? Is the plus upgrade included in the Gen2 kit?  Does the Gen2 kit happen before the INDX upgrade?   I am horribly confused on the execution plan for the parts I have received.  Please advise.

This guide is so confusing.. Why not just include gen2 upgrade steps into the INDX upgrade?? It's extremely difficult to follow the steps of flipping back and forth between guides while the printer is in COMPLETELY different states.

replies.content: +1 to this. Part of the reason I love Prusa printers is just how nice they make their guides, with all the careful images and comments on each step, and then we get stuck with... this, which feels like a pretty severe regression from what we've come to expect.

content: Ahh so for the average Joe/Jane. You notice it will every so often give you something like "until you finish step" or similar. Well if you click on "Contents" on the online guide you can crtl + f whatever step they are referring to. I found this out way too late and it still helped me calm down about missing steps.

replies.content: Okay another tip for the last step "Mount the left side panel back onto the printer. Secure it in place with 3 nylon rivets in the highlighted positions." I could NOT to save my life get the dammed rivets of hell to go in until I propped the bottom two corners up with very thin hex wrenches.

content: There needs to be an index only update, which there is.  A separate Gen2 update, which there is.   Then a combined Gen2 and INDX update which does not exist.  Reading the user notes shows this jumping from one to the other method gets many confused.  The current method of Gen2 and INDX adds hours checking where you are.

A handy note could be inserted after the left side cover is removed "If your printer didn't have a 3DBuddy camera USB cable and you plan on using a 3DBuddy camera, now would be a good time to install that cable."
If I follow this guide, after replacing the pully and belts on the right side, that's it. You don't tell us to bolt the motor back on, nor do you tell us to do the left motor!!

“ Keep following the instructions in the Prusa INDX guide until you finish step 5.16 Securing the zip ties II.”

5.16 is Assembling the Wiper Lock. The mentioned section is 5.7. 

It doesn’t seem like 5.8 through 5.20 ever get done. Is that correct?

Several steps like installation of the bed spacers and of a new sensor would be so much easier if this guide started with removal of both side panels and side covers at the same time right after disconnecting electronics. Printer is lighter, easier to manipulate and easier to seen into that way.
The sequence for tightening the new joints is off, since the front right joint is blocked by the new sensor and the alignment tool can't be used on it.
When you take off the right side panel, if you want to drill it yourself for the expanded bucket that would probably be the perfect time.
